title: Grade 5 French — Mon, May 18
description: Articles & Gender (Les Articles et le Genre) — Last Week Day 1
subject: french

questions.question: In French, every noun has a:
questions.explanation: Every French noun is either masculine (le/un) or feminine (la/une). Unlike English, there is no neutral gender.

questions.question: What is the definite article for a masculine singular noun?
questions.explanation: 'Le' is the definite article (the) for masculine singular nouns. Example: le garçon (the boy), le livre (the book).

questions.question: What is the definite article for a feminine singular noun?
questions.explanation: 'La' is the definite article (the) for feminine singular nouns. Example: la fille (the girl), la table (the table).

questions.question: What article is used for plural nouns (both masculine and feminine)?
questions.explanation: 'Les' = the (plural). It is used for ALL plural nouns regardless of gender: les garçons, les filles.

questions.question: What is the indefinite article for a masculine singular noun?
questions.explanation: 'Un' = a/an (masculine singular). Example: un garçon (a boy), un livre (a book).

questions.question: What article replaces 'le' or 'la' before a vowel or silent 'h'?
questions.explanation: Before vowels or silent 'h', le/la become 'l'' (elision): l'école (the school), l'ami (the friend).

questions.question: Which article means 'some' in French (plural)?
questions.explanation: 'Des' = some (plural indefinite article): des livres (some books), des pommes (some apples).

questions.question: 'Le soleil' — what gender is 'soleil' (sun)?
questions.explanation: 'Le soleil' — 'le' tells us 'soleil' (sun) is masculine. La lune (the moon) is feminine.

questions.question: Which of these nouns is feminine?
questions.explanation: 'La maison' (house) is feminine — 'la' indicates feminine gender.

questions.question: How do you make most French nouns feminine from the masculine form?
questions.explanation: Most French nouns add '-e' to form the feminine: ami → amie, étudiant → étudiante.

questions.question: What is the correct article for 'école' (school)?
questions.explanation: 'L'école' — since 'école' starts with a vowel, 'la' becomes 'l'' (elision). École is feminine.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: '___ enfant' (the child)
questions.explanation: 'L'enfant' — because 'enfant' starts with a vowel, elision occurs. 'Enfant' can be masc. or fem.

questions.question: 'Des livres' contains which type of article?
questions.explanation: 'Des' is the plural indefinite article (some/any). 'Des livres' = some books.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: Je mange le pain (I eat bread/the bread)
Je mange un pain (I eat a bread)
Je mange des pain (I eat some bread)
questions.explanation: 'Je mange le pain' is correct — 'pain' is masculine. 'Je mange du pain' (partitive) also works for 'some bread'.

questions.question: Why is gender important in French?
options: Because articles, adjectives, and agreement all depend on a noun's gender
questions.explanation: Gender affects articles (le/la), adjective agreement (grand/grande), and other parts of the sentence. It is fundamental to French grammar.
